title: On a private plain-HTTP deployment the OAuth authorization-server metadata advertises an https issuer that matches neither the protected-resource metadata nor the token iss
body:
qa#3 · os-tesla · session_01L9qibw6yXcLi9aRRBpPT4W

## Reproduction (8e3d4a54, showcase boot with `OS_AUTH_URL=http://10.0.0.5:PORT`; the link-local `http://169.254.10.20:PORT` behaves the same; loopback is http throughout)

1. `GET /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource` → `authorization_servers: ["http://10.0.0.5:PORT/api/v1/auth"]`.
2. `GET /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server/api/v1/auth` → `issuer: "https://10.0.0.5:PORT/api/v1/auth"`, while the authorization, token and registration endpoints are `http://…`.
3. Run a native-client authorization-code flow with `resource=http://10.0.0.5:PORT/api/v1/mcp` → the callback carries `iss=https://10.0.0.5:PORT/api/v1/auth`; the access-token JWT carries `iss: "http://10.0.0.5:PORT/api/v1/auth"`. The token still serves `tools/list`.

## Expected vs actual

- Expected: one issuer identifier everywhere. RFC 8414 §3.3 requires the metadata `issuer` to equal the identifier it was fetched for, and RFC 9207 / the JWT `iss` must equal it.
- Actual: the AS metadata and the authorize `iss` say https; the PRM and the token say http. A strict MCP client refuses discovery on exactly the private-host deployments `ai.mcp-oauth-private-host-transport` enables. (No real client was run; the client-side effect is inferred from the specs.)

## Mechanism

`@better-auth/oauth-provider` 1.7.12 `validateIssuerUrl` rewrites a non-loopback http issuer to https; plugin-auth's own issuer (`getAuthIssuer`) keeps http.

QA-source: #33081 · ai.mcp-oauth-private-host-transport · observed beside the clauses
